questions.q: Why should an imputer be placed inside a Pipeline rather than applied to the whole dataset first?
options: Pipelines are faster than pandas fillna
So each training fold learns its fill values from training rows only, avoiding leakage
Because imputers only work inside pipelines
So that the test set is filled with zeros
questions.explain: Fill values such as medians are learned parameters. Learning them from all rows lets test-fold information influence training. Inside a pipeline, cross-validation refits the imputer on each fold's training rows.

A row of column averages
Nothing; it only changes the fill strategy
A 0/1 column per feature that had missing values, flagging where gaps were
questions.explain: The indicator columns tell the model which values were originally missing, preserving any signal in the missingness itself.

questions.q: In the lesson, customers missing monthly_charge churned at 57% versus 25%. What does this suggest?
options: Missing values should always be dropped
The median is the best possible fill
The missingness itself is informative, so consider indicator columns
The dataset is too small to use
questions.explain: When the chance of a value being missing depends on the target, the gap carries signal. Indicator columns let the model use it; in the lesson they lifted AUC from 0.760 to 0.798.

questions.q: Which option does scikit-learn 1.1 support that lets some models skip imputation entirely?
options: HistGradientBoostingClassifier accepts NaN values natively
LinearRegression accepts NaN directly
StandardScaler removes NaN automatically
OneHotEncoder fills NaN with the mean
questions.explain: Histogram-based gradient boosting learns how to route missing values at each split. Most linear models and many others still raise an error on NaN.

questions.q: Why is comparing a drop-rows model's score to an imputation model's score misleading?
options: Dropping rows never changes the score
Imputed models cannot be scored
It is evaluated on a different, reduced set of rows, so the scores are not like-for-like
AUC cannot be computed after dropping rows
questions.explain: After dropping rows with gaps, the model is tested only on complete rows, often an easier subset, and it would still fail on future rows that have gaps.
